question: Which offices may read the full text, attached documents and transcripts, event notes and AI summary of an exit interview at each sensitivity level, is the consent of the retiring member a precondition of publication, of reading and of any model or search use, who may record that consent or its withdrawal on the retiree behalf, and who owns the knowledge archive that the published copy lives in?
decision: Enforce the same classification and sensitivity floor across interview list, detail, documents, search, summary and published copies. Publication, semantic indexing and model use each require distinct recorded consent from the retiree and the necessary institutional approval; silence is refusal. An officer may record consent on behalf of retiree only from a verified signed instruction. Revocation blocks future access/use and triggers derived-data review and removal where feasible; legal holds preserve protected evidence. Tenant-designated knowledge custodian owns the archive.
originalProposedDecision: Apply SENSITIVITY_MIN_ROLE everywhere: list, item, documents and the knowledge-base copy. The retiree's consent is required before publication and before any search or model use. The retiree records consent themselves; an admin may record it on their behalf only with an uploaded signed form. The org's admin owns the knowledge archive.
independentApprovalScope: decision wording / platform baseline only; NOT independent security or operational testing
